title: State of Washington v. Lui
questions: Whether a criminal defendant's right to confront witnesses is violated when an expert witness for the State testifies based on a nontestifying expert's report.

title: Camicia v. City of Mercer Island
questions: Whether under the recreational use statute, RCW 4.24.210, the city of Mercer Island is immune from liability for an accident that occurred on a bicycle trail situated on land originally deeded to the city for road or street purposes.

title: State of Washington v. Franklin
questions: Whether the trial court in a prosecution for cyberstalking erroneously disallowed evidence that someone else committed the crime after allowing the alleged other suspect to assert her Fifth Amendment right to remain silent.

title: State of Washington v. Dobbs
questions: Whether in a prosecution for domestic violence offenses the defendant’s conduct toward the victim before and after his arrest supported a ruling that he forfeited his right to challenge the admission of the unavailable victim’s out-of-court statements, even though there was no evidence that the defendant threatened the victim not to testify or direct evidence that the victim refused to appear because of threats.

title: In re Personal Restraint Petition of Stockwell
questions: Whether a personal restraint petitioner alleging that his guilty plea was involuntary because he was misinformed of the maximum sentence must establish actual and substantial prejudice in order to obtain relief.

title: Youngs v. PeaceHealth
questions: Whether under Louden v. Myhre, 110 Wn.2d 675, 756 P.2d 128 (1988), attorneys representing a defendant hospital corporation in a medical malpractice action are prohibited from having ex parte contact with nonparty treating physicians employed by the hospital corporation, and if so, whether Louden was abrogated by amendments to RCW 5.60.060(4) providing that the waiver of the physician-patient privilege for any one physician following the filing of a medical malpractice lawsuit constitutes a waiver of the privilege as to all physicians.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Gomez
questions: Whether the defendant in a prosecution for homicide by abuse and first degree manslaughter was deprived of effective assistance of counsel due to counsel’s inexperience, mishandling of expert testimony, and lack of preparation and administrative support.

title: Wilkinson v. Chiwawa Communities Association
questions: Whether a homeowners association properly amended its covenants to prohibit the short-term rental of homes in light of existing covenants limiting use to single family residences and prohibiting commercial use of properties.

title: State of Washington v. Johnson
questions: Johnson appealed his conviction for driving while license suspended in the third degree (DWLS), claiming that the DWLS law does not criminalize driving with a license suspended for failing to pay traffic fines. He also argued that the State could not constitutionally suspend his license because of his indigence. Finally, he contended that the State must pay the costs of his appeal.

title: State of Washington v. Roden
questions: Does a person have a privacy interest in a text message once it is sent?

title: State of Washington v. Hinton
questions: Did police violate the defendant's constitutionally protected right to privacy when, without a warrant, they observed and responded to the defendant's text messages which appeared on the screen of a third party's wireless device?

title: Ockletree v. Franciscan Health Sys.
questions: Does the exemption for nonprofit religious employers from Washington's law against discrimination violate the state constitution?

title: Rekhter v. Dep't of Soc. & Health Servs.
questions: The Department of Social and Health Services challenges a judgment of more than $90 million after a jury found that the agency breached its contractual duty of good faith and fair dealing toward in-home care providers

title: Fisher Broad. v. City of Seattle
questions: The Seattle Police Department records many of its contacts with people. Did it violate the Public Records Act when it told a reporter that it did not have a list of recordings and would not release the recordings?

title: Schroeder v. Weighall
questions: Whether RCW 4.16.190(2), which eliminates tolling for minors' medical malpractice claims, violates article I, sections 10 and 12 of the Washington Constitution, and the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

title: PT Air Watchers v. Dep't of Ecology
questions: Whether the Department of Ecology, in determining that no environmental impact statement was necessary for a proposed project, failed to adequately consider the effects of carbon dioxide emissions and demand for woody biomass, and whether the project is exempt from the environmental impact statement requirement as part of an energy recovery facility that existed before January 1, 1989

title: AllianceOne Receivables Mgmt., Inc. v. Lewis
questions: When a plaintiff files a lawsuit for damages of $10,000 or less, and later voluntarily dismisses the suit, is the defendant entitled to attorney fees and costs as the prevailing party?

title: Hundtofte v. Encarnacion
questions: May a trial judge order the clerk to replace someone's name with initials in an electronic court docket? If so, when?

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Gentry
questions: The court considers a death-row inmate's claim that his trial was prejudiced by prosecutorial misconduct

title: State of Washington v. Piatnitsky
questions: When a suspect under custodial interrogation tells police "I don't want to talk right now, man," 1) is the suspect more protected under the state constitution than under the federal constitution, and 2) is the suspect's statement an unequivocal invocation of his right to remain silent?

title: Eubanks v. Brown
questions: Must sexual harassment claims against a deputy prosecutor be tried in the county where the harassment occurred?

title: State of Washington v. Deskins
questions: After the defendant was convicted of confining dogs in an unsafe manner, did the trial court have authority to order the defendant to forfeit all of her pets and livestock, pay $21,582 in restitution to the sheriff's office, and live away from all pets and livestock during her two year probationary period?

title: State of Washington v. Jordan
questions: The court considers whether a sentencing court erred in finding that a manslaughter conviction from Texas was legally comparable to a manslaughter conviction from Washington for the purposes of calculating an offender score

title: State of Washington v. Gower
questions: Gower was convicted of incest and indecent liberties at a bench trial. Based on a statute that has since been found unconstitutional, the trial judge admitted evidence of Gower's prior sex crimes. Was that reversible error?

title: State of Washington v. Pena Fuentes
questions: After the defendant's conviction but while a motion for a new trial was pending, a detective listened to phone conversations between the defendant and his attorney. Should the defendant's criminal charges be dismissed with prejudice?

title: State of Washington v. Humphries
questions: Did the trial court err in allowing the defense attorney to stipulate to an element of the charged crime over the objection of the defendant?

title: Ellensburg Cement Prods., Inc. v. Kittitas County
questions: The court must decide: (1) whether Kittitas County's procedure for appealing environmental determinations violated state law; and (2) whether a county board correctly interpreted the county's zoning ordinances to permit gravel processing on agricultural land

title: State of Washington v. K.L.B.
questions: The court must decide: (1) whether a Sound Transit Fare Enforcement Officer whose employment is contracted through a private security firm is a "public servant," and (2) whether the definition of "public servant" is unconstitutionally vague

title: State of Washington v. Garcia
questions: The petitioner asks the court to review the elements of kidnapping in the first degree. He also asks the court to consider whether there was sufficient evidence to sustain a kidnapping conviction, whether his right to present a defense was violated, and whether there was prosecutorial misconduct at trial.

title: In re Det. of Morgan
questions: The court considers whether an accused sexually violent predator (SVP) has a due process right to be competent during an SVP commitment trial, and whether an in-chambers discussion regarding an order to involuntary medicate the petitioner violated his article I, section 10 right to a public trial

title: State of Washington v. Coley
questions: Did the trial court err in placing the burden of proof on competency after an initial finding of incompetency and what is the remedy if the burden is misallocated? Was the defendant denied his right to self-representation?

title: State of Washington v. Kipp
questions: Did the trial court err in admitting into evidence a secretly recorded conversation between Kipp and his brother-in-law in violation of the privacy act?

title: State of Washington v. MacDicken
questions: When police arrested Abraham MacDicken, they moved the stolen bags he was carrying a car's length away and searched them without a warrant. Were the bags too far away for the search to be valid? Can MacDicken challenge a search of stolen property?

title: Jametsky v. Olsen
questions: Washington law protects the owners of distressed properties. The issue before the court is whether a county treasurer must start the tax foreclosure process before a property can be considered distressed because of nonpayment of taxes

title: LK Operating, LLC v. Collection Grp., LLC
questions: Were any attorney ethical rules violated in the formation of a joint business venture agreement, and what are the consequences if they were?

title: LK Operating, LLC v. Collection Grp., LLC
questions: In a legal malpractice case, has the complaining party shown that it suffered any damages?

title: In re Estate of Toland
questions: Whether a Japanese divorce decree should be registered under the doctrine of comity

title: State of Washington v. Koss
questions: The court must decide whether a discussion in private between the judge and counsel about jury instructions violated the defendant's right to a public trial

title: State of Washington v. Shearer
questions: During each of the defendants' criminal trials, one potential juror was questioned in the judge's chambers. Did this violate the constitutional right to a public trial?

title: State of Washington v. Smith
questions: The trial court held sidebar conferences on objections to evidence in a hallway outside the courtroom. This court must decide whether these conferences violated Mr. Smith's right to a public trial.

title: State of Washington v. Frawley
questions: Can a defendant waive his public trial right under the Washington State Constitution?

title: State of Washington v. Njonge
questions: The court considers several questions connected to Njonge's claim that his right to a public trial was violated.

title: State of Washington v. Slert
questions: The Washington State Constitution requires open public trials. Was the constitution violated when four potential jurors were dismissed after an in-chambers review of their answers to a jury questionnaire?

title: Kumar v. Gate Gourmet, Inc.
questions: Does Washington's Law Against Discrimination require employers to make reasonable accommodations for an employee's religious practices?

title: Gray v. Suttell & Assocs.
questions: The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Washington certified the following question to us: Does the pre-2013 definition of "collection agency" in Washington's Collection Agency Act include debt buyers?

title: State of Washington v. Witherspoon
questions: Mr. Witherspoon challenges his robbery conviction and Persistent Offender Accountability Act sentence of life in prison without the possibility of release.

title: Town of Woodway v. Snohomish County
questions: The court considers whether a developer has the vested right to have its permit applications processed under land use ordinances that were found not to comply with the State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) after the developer submitted its complete applications

title: Wash. Educ. Ass'n v. Dep't of Ret. Sys.
questions: Could the State Legislature lawfully eliminate investment fund "gain-sharing" from some public pension plans?

title: Ralph v. Dep't of Natural Res.
questions: The court considers whether tort actions seeking monetary damages for injuries to real property fall within the scope of RCW 4.12.010 and, if so, whether the statute's filing requirements relate to jurisdiction or venue

title: Anaya Gomez v. Sauerwein
questions: The court decides whether a patient can sue a health care provider under Washington's informed consent law for not informing the patient about a lab test result that the provider mistakenly believed was a false positive.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of McNeil
questions: Should the Petitioners' sentences for murders they committed as juveniles be changed based on the recent U.S. Supreme Court case of Miller v. Alabama?

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Petersen
questions: This case asks whether the Certified Professional Guardianship Board can discipline Lori Petersen for her decisions made on behalf of three of her wards

title: State of Washington v. Johnson
questions: This case presents two issues: (1) whether the information charging the crime of unlawful imprisonment must include elements found in the definition of "restrain," and, if so, whether the information in this case fairly included those elements; and (2) whether defense counsel provided effective assistance by proposing that the jury instructions include a generic definition of "reckless" for the crime of assault in the second degree

title: In re the Personal Restraint Petition of
questions: Is the petitioner entitled to have his assault conviction vacated based on double jeopardy principles?

title: Storti v. Univ. of Wash.
questions: Did the University of Washington breach a contractual obligation to its faculty by cancelling, in March of 2009, the 2% "merit pay" raises scheduled to take effect in the 2009-10 academic year?

title: State of Washington v. Owens
questions: Does RCW 9A.82.050(1) describe alternative means of committing first degree trafficking in stolen property, and if so, is there substantial evidence to support each of the alternative means?

title: Campbell v. Dep't of Emp't Sec.
questions: Did the agency err in denying Campbell unemployment benefits under RCW 50.20.050(2)(b)(iii), the "quit to follow" provision

title: Riverview Cmty. Grp. v. Spencer & Livingston
questions: Should the court dismiss a claim seeking to force the defendants to operate a golf course at a financial loss because the relief sought is too harsh?

title: Schmidt v. Coogan
questions: This case presents multiple issues relating to legal malpractice claims, including the collectibility of an underlying judgment and available damages

title: BAC Home Loans Servicing, LP v. Fulbright
questions: The court considers whether a party is a valid redemptioner when the party recorded its lien before a condominium association brought a judicial foreclosure action

title: LaCoursiere v. Camwest Dev., Inc.
questions: The court must decide whether bonuses, once paid, are wages and if so, whether an employer's profit sharing plan violated the Wage Rebate Act

title: State of Washington v. Lindsay
questions: Defendants Lindsay and Holmes were convicted of first degree burglary and robbery, among other things, at a joint trial. The court must decide whether some of the prosecutor's remarks during trial amounted to misconduct that influenced the jury.

title: Outsource Servs. Mgmt. v. Nooksack Bus. Corp.
questions: Does a state court have jurisdiction over a contract claim involving an Indian tribe when that tribe waived its sovereign immunity?

title: State of Washington v. Crumpton
questions: For a motion for postconviction DNA testing, should the court have to presume the DNA results would be favorable to the convicted individual when deciding whether performing the test might demonstrate that person's innocence?

title: Walston v. Boeing Co.
questions: Is Walston's personal injury action against Boeing for damages stemming from workplace asbestos exposure exempt from the Industrial Insurance Act's exclusive remedy provision on the basis that Boeing deliberately intended the injury?

title: In re Estate of Hambleton
questions: Whether the 2013 amendments to the Estate and Transfer Act may be applied retroactively.

title: State of Washington v. Medina
questions: Does participation in a King County Community Center Alternative Program constitute "partial confinement," for which an offender is entitled to credit for time served prior to sentencing?

title: Frias v. Asset Foreclosure Servs., Inc.
questions: The Deeds of Trust Act governs nonjudicial foreclosures. Can a person sue for violations of the Deeds of Trust Act before any foreclosure sale has been completed?

title: State of Washington v. Lamar
questions: The defendant argues that the trial court's error, failure to instruct the jury to begin deliberations anew after an alternate juror replaced a juror who was ill, is manifest constitutional error that may be raised for the first time on appeal.

title: State of Washington v. Russell
questions: Under what circumstances may a police officer frisk a suspect for weapons, and whether that police officer may search a small container found during the frisk?

title: State of Washington v. Barton
questions: Was the trial court's order requiring the defendant to post 10 percent of his bail amount in cash or other security constitutionally permissible?

title: State of Washington v. France
questions: France was convicted of felony harassment. The jury was instructed "threat also means" conduct not proven. Under the law of the case doctrine, should the court reverse his convictions?

title: Expedia, Inc. v. Steadfast Ins. Co.
questions: Did the trial court err in delaying ruling on Zurich's duty to defend Expedia from third-party lawsuits pending further discovery of facts relevant to the issue of coverage?

title: Durland v. San Juan County
questions: Whether neighboring landowners can challenge the issuance of a building permit under 42 U.S.C. §1983 or the Land Use Petition Act? Whether attorney's fees are available under RCW 4.84.370 when a party prevails on jurisdictional grounds?

title: State of Washington v. Villanueva-Gonzalez
questions: Was double jeopardy violated when Villanueva-González was convicted of two different assault charges for multiple actions against the same victim in a short time frame?

title: In re Marriage of Chandola
questions: This case concerns the parenting plan entered in the parties' dissolution proceeding. The petitioner argues that plan exceeded the trial court's authority because it imposed severe restrictions on his contact with his young daughter

title: Scrivener v. Clark College
questions: Whether the trial court properly granted summary judgment to the employer in an age discrimination case

title: State of Washington v. W.R.
questions: The Court considers whether a defendant may be assigned the burden of proving consent as a defense to a charge of rape by forcible compulsion, in light of the Due Process Clause

title: FutureSelect Portfolio Management , et al. v. Tremont Group Holdings
questions: This case asks whether (1) the laws of Washington or those of New York apply to the dispute; (2) Oppenheimer has sufficient contacts with Washington to give our courts power over it; and (3) Ernst and Young can be a seller under the Washington state securities act.

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Coggin
questions: Whether the defendant in a criminal prosecution was deprived of his right to a public trial when some prospective jurors were examined in chambers, and if so, whether the defendant must show actual and substantial prejudice from the violation in order to obtain relief by personal restraint petition.

title: In re Pers. Restraint of Speight
questions: Whether the defendant in a criminal prosecution was deprived of his right to a public trial when some prospective jurors were examined in chambers, and if so, whether the defendant must show actual and substantial prejudice from the violation in order to obtain relief by personal restraint petition

title: State of Washington v. Peltier
questions: Can a criminal defendant waive the statute of limitations?

title: In Re Pers. Restraint of Thomas
questions: Does the rule announced by the U.S. Supreme Court in Miller v. Alabama, prohibiting mandatory sentences of life without parole for juveniles, apply to a juvenile offender sentenced to 999 months in prison?

title: State of Washington v. Hawkins
questions: Did the trial court properly grant a new trial due to newly discovered evidence? And, did the new date set for trial violate the defendant's right to a speedy trial?

title: SentinelC3 v. Hunt
questions: Did the shareholders submit enough evidence at trial to defeat the corporation's motion for summary judgment on the value of their shares?

title: State of Washington v. Sykes
questions: Should drug court staffings be presumptively open to the public under the Washington State Constitution?

title: State of Washington v. Gunderson
questions: Were the defendant's past acts of domestic violence admissible to help the jury assess the credibility of the alleged victim, who testified that no assault occurred

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Hall
questions: Whether the Disciplinary Broad erred in affirming the appellant's two-year suspension from the practice of law following a disciplinary proceeding concerning the appellant's creation and management of an elderly woman's estate.

title: Moore v. Health Care Auth.
questions: A judge found that the State improperly denied health benefits to certain part-time employees. How should the judge determine the value of those denied health benefits?

title: State of Washington v. Davis
questions: The petitioners were convicted of rendering criminal assistance to Maurice Clemmons after he killed four Lakewood Police Officers. They were also convicted of possessing one of the slain officer's service pistols. The court must decide whether the State presented sufficient evidence at trial that the petitioners illegally possessed the stolen firearm and whether the "destructive impact on a person other than the victim" sentence aggravator applies to the petitioners' convictions for rendering criminal assistance

title: Lyons v. U.S. Bank Nat'l Ass'n
questions: Whether a borrower can bring claims under the Deed of Trust Act and/or the Consumer Protection Act when the property was not sold and whether summary judgment dismissal of Lyons' claims was improper.

title: Becerra Becerra v. Expert Janitorial, LLC
questions: Employers are required to pay those they employ at least minimum wage and overtime. Determining whether someone is actually "employed" by an entity requires a court to consider a variety of factors. The court must decide if the trial court considered the right factors in determining whether Fred Meyer and Expert Janitorial employed the plaintiffs

title: State of Washington v. Berg
questions: Is a kidnapping charge supported by sufficient evidence if the conduct constituting kidnapping is merely incidental to a separate charge of robbery?

title: Cashmere Valley Bank v. Dep't of Revenue
questions: Whether Cashmere Valley can claim a tax deduction under RCW 82.04.4292 for interest income from investments in mortgage-backed securities?

title: State of Washington v. Quaale
questions: Whether a police officer's opinion that a defendant accused of DUI was "impaired" amounted to an improper opinion on the defendant's guilt

title: Johnston-Forbes v. Matsunaga
questions: Whether the trial court properly admitted expert biomechanical testimony in an automobile collision case.

title: State of Washington v. Williams
questions: The court considers whether sentencing courts have the authority to count separately prior convictions committed during the commission of a burglary in calculating a defendant's offender score notwithstanding a finding that they involved the same criminal conduct

title: City of Lakewood v. Koenig
questions: Did the city of Lakewood violate the Public Records Act by inadequately explaining to David Koenig why it redacted driver's license numbers from the records he requested? If so, is Koenig entitled to attorney fees?

title: A.G., by and through his parents, J.G. and K.G., et al. v. Premera Blue Cross
questions: Does the definition of "mental health services" in the Mental Health Parity Act include medically necessary neurodevelopmental therapies when the therapies are used to treat mental disorders?

title: O.S.T. v. Regence BlueShield
questions: Does the definition of "mental health services" in the Mental Health Parity Act include medically necessary neurodevelopmental therapies when the therapies are used to treat mental disorders?

title: Failla v. FixtureOne Corp.
questions: Do Washington courts have personal jurisdiction over an officer of a nonresident corporation that employs a Washington resident?

title: Anderson v. Dussault
questions: Does the finality of court approved trust accountings under the Trustees' Accounting Act, chapter 11.106 RCW, bar petitioner's breach of trust suit that would otherwise be timely brought under the Trust and Estate Dispute Resolution Act, chapter 11.96A RCW?

title: Sixty-01 Ass'n of Apt. Owners v. Parsons
questions: Can a third party purchaser of a condominium at a sheriff's sale withdraw his or her winning bid before the sale is confirmed by the court or is a creditor entitled to confirmation unless substantial irregularities are proved?

title: State of Washington v. McEnroe
questions: Is the absence of sufficient mitigating circumstances to merit leniency an element of capital murder in Washington, which the State must allege in the charging information?

title: In Re Det. of D.W.
questions: Counties have the power to involuntarily detain people who are mentally ill and dangerous for evaluation and treatment. A trial judge found it was illegal and unconstitutional to detain such people in hospital rooms without evaluation or treatment when there was no space in evaluation and treatment facilities. Should the court affirm or reverse?

title: State of Washington v. A.G.S.
questions: Whether a psychological evaluation of a juvenile sex offender's amenability to treatment must be kept confidential

title: State of Washington v. LEWIS
questions: The court must decide whether a prosecutor's remarks during closing argument violated the rights of the defendant

title: In Re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Jones
questions: The court must decide whether to adopt the Washington State Bar Association Disciplinary Board's recommendation to disbar Russell Kenneth Jones

title: Grove v. Peacehealth St. Joseph Hosp.
questions: Did the courts below err in determining that the patient did not meet his burden under the medical malpractice statute, Ch. 7.70 RCW, to show negligent conduct by particular members of his hospital care team and by failing to apply Hansch v. Hackett, 190 Wn. 97, 66 P.2d 1129 (1937), which predated enactment of RCW 7.70?

title: Moore v. Steve's Outboard Serv.
questions: Is it a nuisance per se to operate a business without a necessary permit?

title: State of Washington v. Andy
questions: Was Joey Andy's right to a public trial violated when his trial lasted into the evening past the posted courthouse hours?

W.G. Clark Constr. Co. v. Pac. Nw. Reg'l Council of Carpenters
In re Pers. Restraint of Yates
In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Jackson
Powers v. WB Mobile Servs., Inc.
In re Pers. Restraint of McWilliams
